description: Layer 2 - Security: Remove JWT_SECRET default value (force explicit configuration), fix KeyVault access policies to use Azure RBAC
steps: In apps/backend/app/config.py: Change JWT_SECRET from having a default value of 'CHANGE_ME_IN_PRODUCTION_AT_LEAST_32_CHARS_LONG' to having NO default (make it a required field). Change the line to: JWT_SECRET: str (no default). This forces ALL environments to explicitly set JWT_SECRET - no more insecure fallback for staging/dev. Also update the validate_production_secrets validator: keep the length check but remove the check for the specific default string since there's no default anymore.

In infra/azure/shared-resources.bicep: Replace the empty accessPolicies array with Azure RBAC authorization. Add 'enableRbacAuthorization: true' to the KeyVault properties and remove the 'accessPolicies: []' line. This allows Azure role assignments (like 'Key Vault Secrets User') to control access instead of the legacy access policy model.
acceptance_criteria: apps/backend/app/config.py no longer has a default value for JWT_SECRET
The validate_production_secrets method no longer checks for the old default string
infra/azure/shared-resources.bicep KeyVault no longer has accessPolicies: []
Python config file parses without syntax errors
verification: Run: grep -n 'CHANGE_ME' apps/backend/app/config.py && echo 'FAIL' || echo 'OK: no default JWT secret'
Run: grep 'accessPolicies' infra/azure/shared-resources.bicep && echo 'FAIL: accessPolicies still present' || echo 'OK'
